The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
The U.S. Army is calling the controlled explosion of roughly five tons of hazardous chemicals
in southeastern Iowa a success.
People living near the plant are worried that lead dust from the blast could reach their
homes and farms, putting their health at risk.
NPR's Kat Lanstorf reports.
Military explosive experts detonated more than 60 barrels of unstable lead azide at
the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middleton, Iowa.
At a press conference shortly afterward, Major General Eric Shirley, who led the Army operation,
said the operation had "exceeded expectations."
I believe, absolutely, that we reduced as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible

It could be several days before experts know whether or how much lead dust was released
into the surrounding environment.
Kat Lanstorf, NPR News.
U.S. intelligence officials have briefed congressional staff on a Chinese woman who had an affair
with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang.
NPR's Ryan Lucas reports officials discuss the woman's ties to China's spy services.
The intelligence officials told Congress there is no evidence that Alice Wong, who had an
affair with the NVIDIA boss, is a Chinese spy or an asset of the country's intelligence
services.
There is also no evidence that she began the affair in order to gather intelligence for
China, although she is believed to have passed long information once the romantic relationship
began.
That's according to a person familiar with the matter who was granted anonymity to discuss
a closed-door briefing.
There is more evidence that her associate, Kang Wei, has ties to China's Ministry of
State Security.
While Jensen Huang's affair has generated headlines, experts say the bigger national
security issue is the diversion of NVIDIA's most advanced AI chips to China.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
The Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City has been moved to Saturday.
It's the first time in history that the event has been postponed.
A powerful storm developing along the East Coast is forecast to bring strong winds and
heavy rain to Manhattan tomorrow morning, making it unsafe to fly the giant balloons.
The same storm has prompted a statewide emergency in New Jersey.
Governor Mikey Sherrill says the strongest wing gusts are expected along the shore.
The entire state will see high winds all day tomorrow, with frequent gusts up to 70 miles
per hour along the coast and 60 miles per hour inland.
On the West Coast, unusually high tides are prompting coastal flood warnings in parts
of California, Oregon, and Washington.
Rain is expected to continue in the Pacific Northwest on Thanksgiving with snow in the
mountains.
This is NPR News.
Americans are getting more comfortable with using artificial intelligence to help plan
their Thanksgiving dinners.
But as NPR's Chloe Veltman reports, many people still remain skeptical.
According to a trends report from the Food Industry Association published earlier this
month, 65 percent of Thanksgiving shoppers say they'd like to use AI to do things like
scope out holiday recipes or festive ideas and learn new cooking skills.

Senior League Baseball is asking a federal judge in New York City to rule that a lockout
team owners are considering for next week would be legal under federal antitrust law.

I still love the story of an UpFirst listener who told me that she had cut off all of her
